brief: DB argues last week's inflation data did not clear the bar for further progress towards target, so the Fed hikes on Wednesday. August core CPI came in at +0.29% versus +0.22% in July, about a tenth above DB's forecast, with a 5.9% rise in wireless services alone adding 10bps, plus lodging away (+2.4%) and airfare (+2.7%) gains DB had flagged. Thursday's PPI also skewed hawkish, so DB tracks August core PCE at +0.27%, a pace inconsistent with further progress, and upcoming PCE methodology changes add a couple of basis points more. The only expected statement change is the funds target raised to 3 3/4 to 4 percent, with the SEP median showing one more hike this year and some participants three or more across 2026-2027. Warsh is expected to justify the hike while still eschewing forward guidance. DB recently added a third 25bp hike and now expects 75bps of tightening in total, in September, December and next March, unwinding last year's risk management cuts. Risks are two-sided: October is possible if data trends hold, while softer inflation or labor data or tighter financial conditions cut the other way. Wednesday's retail sales are forecast to rebound, headline +0.9% against -0.6%.
